components.cost_effect: Known-domain projection adds no original query; the block estimate controls the sum of distance-sensitive inner costs.
components.goal: Reduce aggregate true inner starting distances.
components.key_estimate: For r_t=||wt-P_eta(xt)||, r0,r1<=3R and sum_{t=k}^ell r_t^2<=256 R^2(1+H_{2k})^2/k^2 for k>=2 and k<=ell<=min(2k-1,K). This is an aggregate block estimate, not a pointwise O(k^-3/2) guarantee.
components.name: Projected linear warm start
components.operation: Project 2 yhat_{t-1}-yhat_{t-2} onto the original X; retain the ordinary anchored Halpern update for xt.
components.requires: One fixed eta and hence one fixed firmly nonexpansive analytical resolvent P_eta throughout the orbit; certified inner errors <=e.
transfer_checks: Changing eta during a run requires a new orbit analysis.
Mere nonexpansiveness does not provide the firm-nonexpansive dissipative estimate.
Approximate projections or inner certificates need separate error and normal-membership accounting.

components.cost_effect: Includes every inner solve and no additional final F query.
components.goal: Make invalid distance trials finite while preserving sound successful outputs.
components.key_estimate: Under a valid promise the total uncapped inner cost is below the installed cap; Lemma 7.2 bounds the returned tangent certificate.
components.name: Nested cap and saved-value acceptance
components.operation: Use U_a and B above, interrupt before a forbidden original query, retain the final genuine normal and subtract the known affine term from the saved G value.
components.requires: Certified inner interface and every active ancestor counter propagated through descendants.

content.family: Projected extrapolated warm starts for inexact Halpern iteration

limitations.statement: Guaranteed success needs a valid supplied distance. A false promise may cause Failure but never permits an unchecked successful certificate.
Block energy does not assert pointwise accelerated second differences or constant cost for each inner solve.

model.domain_and_norm: Known nonempty compact convex X subset R^d, diam(X)<=D, x0 in X; Euclidean vector norm and induced multilinear operator norm. N_X(x)={n:<n,u-x><=0 for every u in X}.
model.information: Public: X,d,p,Lp,D,x0,R,epsilon and an already constructed S_gamma,b with fixed known constant C_S. Hidden: a solution, actual distances and unknown operator beyond returned jets. Exact feasible order-p queries return F,DF,...,D^(p-1)F. Exact known-domain projections and known Taylor-model operations are internal information-model operations.
model.operator: Fixed integer p>=2; Lp,D>0. Unknown F is C^(p-1) on an open neighborhood of X, monotone on X, with Lip(D^(p-1)F)<=Lp. No bounds on lower derivatives or F values and no positive strong monotonicity of F are assumed.

performance_links.scope_note: Theorem 8.1: S_gamma,b to A_alpha,b+4 under the stated exponent range, certified interface and original-query accounting.

variants.cost: Exactly K+1 certified inner solves are scheduled, including startup t=0,1 and final t=K. Count every original-F query in all descendants, failed radius trials and certificate evaluations. One Gt jet uses one original-F jet plus known affine data; for p>=2 this does not increase Lp. Recovering the final saved F value and its norm test require no additional query. The explicit cap is finite even for an invalid distance promise and is O_p((1+Q_R^alpha)L_A(R,epsilon)^(b+4)), with L_A=1+log(2+D/R+Q_R), for the fixed interface. No arithmetic or bit-complexity bound is asserted.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Original PDF Algorithm 5 p.20; equations (7.1)–(7.5), (8.1)–(8.4); Sections 7–8 pp.19–23.
variants.name: ExtrapolatedHalpern(S_gamma,b,F,x0,R,epsilon)
variants.output: Failure or (yhatK,nK,F(yhatK)) with yhatK in X, nK in the original N_X(yhatK), evaluated F(yhatK), and tested norm <=epsilon. Return yhatK, not xK. A valid distance promise guarantees completion and success under the stated interfaces.
public_inputs: Certified S_gamma,b and its known leading constant C_S
variants.query_and_update: For t=0,...,K inclusive: w0=x0; w1=yhat0; for t>=2 set wt=Pi_X(2 yhat_{t-1}-yhat_{t-2}). Define Gt(z)=F(z)+(z-xt)/eta and call S_gamma,b(Gt,wt,1/eta,delta). Receive (yhatt,nt,Gt(yhatt)) with nt in N_X(yhatt) and ||Gt(yhatt)+nt||<=delta. If a cap interrupts or the required certified call fails, return Failure. For t<K set x_{t+1}=[x0+(t+1)yhatt]/(t+2). After t=K compute F(yhatK)=GK(yhatK)-(yhatK-xK)/eta from saved data. Test ||F(yhatK)+nK||<=epsilon and return the saved triple only when the test passes; otherwise return Failure.
variants.requirements: The supplied distance promise is that some VI solution zstar satisfies ||x0-zstar||<=R. It is required for guaranteed success, not for sound acceptance or the finite cap. The strong interface returns a feasible genuine normal certificate and evaluated G(y), with cost C_S[1+(Lp r^(p-1)/mu)^gamma]L_S(mu,delta)^b, where r is the unknown actual initial solution distance. It is not supplied to the solver. L_S(mu,delta)=1+log(2+Lp D^(p-1)/mu+Lp D^p/delta+mu D/delta).
variants.state_and_initialization: Define Q_R=Lp R^p/epsilon, alpha=gamma/(1+gamma), K=max{2,ceil(Q_R^alpha)}. H_0=0 and H_m=sum_{i=1}^m 1/i. Set e=R/(K+2)^4, eta=8R(1+H_{K+1})/[epsilon(K+1)], delta=e/eta. Keep eta fixed throughout this entire run, including all K+1 inner solves. Initialize at x0 and retain the two previous approximate proximal outputs and saved operator values.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Install a=(p-1)gamma and U_a(K)=2*3^a+16^a sum_{j=1}^{floor(log_2 K)}(1+H_{2^{j+1}})^a 2^{j(1-3a/2)}. Install B=ceil(C_S L_S(1/eta,e/eta)^b [K+1+(eta Lp)^gamma R^a U_a(K)])+1. Before every original-F query, charge every active ancestor cap, including this B, through a shared interruptible descendant counter. A depleted cap aborts its capped call before the next query; the exhaustion branch is not a delayed check after an uncontrolled subroutine returns. B depends only on public parameters and finite known sums.

summary: Transforms an already available distance-sensitive strong solver into a capped monotone-VI residual solver using projected linear prediction and inexact Halpern updates. The returned point is the last computed approximate proximal point with its genuine evaluated normal certificate.
title: Algorithm 5: ExtrapolatedHalpern with a fixed regularization and interruptible query cap
use_when: An established S_gamma,b interface is available and 2/3<=(p-1)gamma<=2.
Need finite, sound behavior for supplied distance guesses; ordinary Halpern residual estimates alone do not provide this complete certified routine.
